Dogfood & UX QA Pass — native app on emulator

Date: 2026-08-27 · Build: debug assembleDebug at HEAD (main, lastUpdateTime 08:17) · Device: webnovel_api36 emulator (API 36, phone profile, Obsidian theme) · Package com.vinicius741.webnovelarchiver.nativeapp.debug · Data: owner’s real sandbox library — 168 novels, dozens downloaded — used read-mostly; only reversible/test-scoped mutations performed (2 chapters downloaded, 1 test tab created & removed, theme switched & restored, 2 QA backups made & deleted).

TL;DR

I drove every screen the app exposes, exercised the flows a daily reader touches (browse, search/filter, tabs, organize, open/download chapters, read with TTS, EPUB generate/read attempts, trends, AI controls, settings incl. backup, add-story validation), and recorded no crashes and zero ANRs anywhere in logcat. Core reading flows are solid. The problems are concentrated in exactly the place your instinct pointed:

  • The app is heavy on expert-facing exposition. AI Controls (F3) is the worst offender — repeated boilerplate, raw model IDs, internal “spike” jargon. Voice & Speech (F4) asks users to type magic decimal numbers.
  • Progress feedback is weak where work is actually slow. Cold start shows an unlabeled spinner for ~5s (F1, with a scary-but-transient 24–84s degradation episode captured mid-session), and Create Full Backup (F2) dims a row for half a minute and reports success through a system share sheet that auto-closed itself here.
  • A dozen P3 nits (clipped “All” tab, “Index N” noise, inconsistent danger styling, naming mismatches, EPUB dead-ends, Trends emptiness…).

All 12 findings below include screenshots or video taken at the moment of the issue.

F1 · Cold start shows an unlabeled spinner for ~5s baseline — and degraded to 24–84s during part of this session P2 · degraded primary path

The app draws its first frame fast (ActivityTaskManager reports Displayed … +900ms), but that frame is an empty page with a tiny centered spinner while the whole library JSON hydrates. On this emulator with a 168-novel library I measured ≈5–7s of spinner before any content on every cold start, across all screens (Library, Queue, Settings…). There is no skeleton UI, no branding, no progress hint — just blank.

Worse, after running Create Full Backup twice mid-session, subsequent cold starts degraded dramatically: the Downloads screen held the spinner for 24 seconds, and one Library start took 84 seconds. During those windows the app process sat at 0% CPU (blocked, not working) while the emulator was under heavy memory pressure (~157MB free, ~900MB swapped). The state recovered on its own within minutes and cold starts returned to ~5s. Correlation documented; root cause not pinned in this pass.

Logcat every cold start also spams dozens of StrictMode main-thread disk-read violations from AppStorage/DownloadEngine/DevColdStartHooks — consistent with the known whole-file-JSON + global-lock storage architecture noted in the 2026-08-26 performance audit.

F2 · “Create Full Backup” feedback loop is opaque; completion rides on a share sheet that can flash by unnoticed; interrupted backups leak .tmp files P2 · degraded primary path

Tapping Create Full Backup dims the row with a micro-spinner and no progress info while a 37MB ZIP of 168 novels is written (~9–30s+). Completion feedback is only the system share sheet — which on this emulator launched and auto-closed itself within ~1s (logcat: ChooserActivity opened then STOP/DESTROY when nothing can handle the zip); between my screen polls I never caught it visible except on the recorded video frames.

I also confirmed the failure mode where backup #2/#3 taps are silently dead while a previous run's state has not reset, and that an interrupted run leaves an orphaned webnovel_full_backup_*.zip.tmp.2 (37MB) behind with no cleanup and no user-visible trace. The finished zip lives inside app-private storage (files/webnovel_archiver/backups/) — unless the share sheet succeeds, users get no persistent “where is my backup” affordance.

Note: both backup artifacts created during this QA run were deleted afterwards; only pre-existing files remain.

F3 · AI Controls screen is a wall of expert knobs and leaked research jargon P2 · degraded primary path

This single scroll contains three separate model pickers (cover image, rewrite model, verifier model), each followed by the same two-line caution paragraph repeated three times verbatim. Model choices render raw provider IDs (x-ai/grok-imagine-image-2.0, openai/gpt-5.6-terra). Copy leaks internal experiment language straight into product UI (“Verified in the spike: gpt-5.6-terra/sol (lowest drift) …”) plus awkward wording (“an independent check is what makes a draft appliable”). Nothing here indicates defaults or hides advanced options — exactly the “way too complicated” feel this report was asked to hunt. Suggested direction: ship safe defaults up front (one Generate action), collapse model/strength/verifier behind an “Advanced” disclosure, say each rule once.

F4 · Voice & Speech: pitch/rate typed as free-text decimals; voices shown as raw engine IDs P2 · degraded primary path

Pitch and Rate are plain number fields — no sliders, steppers, range hints, presets, or a Reset button, so finding a comfortable speed is trial-and-error typing (default rate ships as 1.8, which reads arbitrary). The chosen voice is displayed as the engine string en-us-x-sfg-local, meaningless to readers, and the save button says “Save TTS” instead of Save. This is a small screen doing developer UX.

F5 · Library tab row clips the last tab (“All”) to a ~20px sliver P3 · polish

At phone width the horizontal tab strip renders Starter/Plan/Reading/Following/Paused fully but leaves “All” as a sliver pinned to the right edge — trivially missable, and nothing signals it scrolls. Either reserve width for the last chip, make the overflow obvious (fade edge), or drop to an overflow menu on narrow screens.

F6 · Chapter list rows waste their subtitle line on “Index N” P3 · polish

In Details’ chapter list, un-downloaded rows show “Index 1”, “Index 2”, … beneath titles — a value-free echo of the row position already given by the number column. Downloaded rows prove the slot can earn its keep (“Index 81 · Downloaded Aug 10, 2026”); un-downloaded ones should carry something useful too (published date, read/unread marker) or nothing.

Collapsed details — every row repeats Index N

F7 · Destructive-action styling is inconsistent across surfaces P3 · polish

The Organize Novels bottom bar paints Delete red with a trash icon, and Details’ overflow marks Delete Novel red — but the Library long-press story dialog lists a plain, accent-neutral Delete directly beneath Select Multiple. Same stakes, different risk signaling, and the worst-placed instance is the least-styled one.

F8 · “Select Multiple” menu item lands on a screen titled “Organize Novels” P3 · polish

Long-press → Select Multiple opens a screen whose header is Organize Novels (which Settings also links to by that name). Same tool, two names depending on entry point; newcomers have to guess they met the same feature twice. Pick one name for the verb everywhere.

F9 · EPUB export dead-ends without a reader app installed — and offers no Share from the EPUB Files screen P3 · polish

Generate works well (with a clear “80 of 90 will be skipped — generate anyway?” prompt). But on a device without an EPUB-capable app, Read EPUB stops at “Install an EPUB reader…” and the EPUB Files card’s only actions are See/Delete — no Share-from-here, which is the universal Android egress. Filename also arrives fully lowercased (a saga of tanya the chansey Ch81-90.epub) next to properly-cased metadata.

F10 · “Large Screen Layout: Auto / Cover / Inner” is jargon on non-foldables P3 · polish

The chips reuse vocabulary from the removed dead “EPUB Volume Folding” control (regression check passed — this is a different, live setting consumed by HostUi) — but to anyone on a slab phone neither “Cover” nor “Inner” means anything, and the explainer sentence doesn’t disambiguate them. Rename to concrete outcomes (e.g. Two-pane on large screens: Auto / Outer-pane cover / Inner detail…) or hide the whole row when the device never folds.

F11 · Trends: duplicated heading and a mostly-empty viewport for sparse novels P3 · polish

For a novel with two snapshots the screen stacks app-bar title, then repeats novel+author as a giant header, shows one flat chart scaled over an axis range (3.8–4.8) that makes a +0.00 change look eventful, and devotes the remaining ~55% of the viewport to emptiness. Minor next to the metric gaps, but the wasted space and double header read unfinished.

F12 · Assorted polish: lingering keyboard, tall Manage-Tabs cards P3 · polish

  • Clearing the library search keeps the keyboard up and focus in the field, hiding the bottom of the grid you came back to browse.
  • Manage Tabs gives every tab a second full-width row for four icon buttons (up/down/edit/delete) with large dead space — five tabs stretch past a screenful; compact per-row actions would halve it.
  • Moving tabs uses arrow icons rather than drag, unusual for Android reordering.

Not run / limitations

  • Live followed-novel sync, mass chapter downloads, deliberately-triggered Cloudflare challenges (third-party mutation avoided per QA policy).
  • Real OpenRouter AI generations (cost discipline; models/copies reviewed statically).
  • Landscape, tablet/large-screen and foldable layouts; release build on physical phone; import/restore/clear-storage flows left untouched (destructive).
  • F1’s root cause: the 24–84s episode was observed and instrumented (idle-blocked process under swap pressure) but not reproduced on demand; treat the causal link to backup I/O as a hypothesis for profiling, not a conclusion.
  • QA-methodology caveat surfaced twice today: on this emulator screencap/uiautomator occasionally return stale/blank frames minutes into a session — several suspected “app bugs” dissolved under pixel-vs- dump cross-checks and were excluded from this report (screen transitions measured ≤0.6s on video; state consistency verified before filing anything).
